title: No two-round minimal line-percolating set in PG(2,5): a counterexample to Conjecture 20 of Gerbner-Keszegh-Meszaros-Patkos-Vizer (arXiv:1608.00531)
beyond_target: accepted after the campaign target of 40 was reached (additional result #45 toward 60)
exact_endpoint: Percolation.not_conjecture20_unconditional : ¬ Percolation.Conjecture20, where Conjecture20 := for every q, every finite projective plane P of order q (literal incidence axioms with a quadrangle) and every r with 4 <= r <= q there is an infection a with Minimal P r a (percolates and no proper subset percolates) and TimeIs P r a 2 (full at round 2 and not earlier), for synchronous r-threshold line percolation
scope: Conjecture 20 fails at the allowed boundary (q,r) = (5,5): in PG(2,5) no inclusion-minimal percolating set has percolation time 2 at threshold 5.

substantive_reason: It refutes a published conjecture on the minimal percolation time of minimal percolating sets in finite projective planes, at a genuine instance (two-round minimal sets exist at (4,4), (5,4), (7,4), (7,5); the source's own three-round construction does not reach (5,5)). The nonexistence is a computer-assisted theorem: a symmetry-normalized SAT encoding refuted by a 129,671-step RUP certificate, kernel-replayed in Lean by a proved bitmask checker with a fully proved semantic bridge and collineation normalization.
